clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-184]: "The Forbidden Fruit's earned damage disappears if the item is removed or rerolled."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:267-284 uses the item once, removes it with RemoveCollectible, re-evaluates the damage cache and requires the damage to stay within 0.05 of the held value. Only the removal path is exercised; a reroll is not.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-191], sentence 2: "three red-heart containers and only half a red heart ... the item is supposed to leave one full red heart after reducing the containers"
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:285-296 requires max=2, red=2, soul=0 and a living player.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-191], sentence 3: "only one red-heart container: using the item on half a heart kills them instead of filling that final container"
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:302-312 requires max=2, red=2, soul=0 and not IsDead() in the same frame as the use.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-303]: "Each later use is meant to add a smaller, diminishing stat increase rather than no increase at all."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:315-358. tragic_mushroom_repeat requires the second use to raise damage, speed and range by > 0.05; tragic_mushroom_diminishing requires the third gain to be > 0.05 and smaller than the second for all three stats. See known_issues[1] for the speed cap.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-311]: "each activation in the current room should add another ten"
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:360-381 requires +10 after the first and +20 after the second activation.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-311], last sentence: "The whole temporary stack should continue to reset on entering another room."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:972-975 compares Luck with the baseline only after Anamnesis has replaced Mutant Clover in the active slot (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:383-385) and after a whole floor change. Exodus gates the bonus on HasCollectible, so Luck returns to the baseline even if the room reset is deleted; the case cannot detect a broken reset.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-318]: "a fresh copy must not inherit a full foreign charge"
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:383-390. The foreign charge is simulated by AddCollectible(Anamnesis, 6) plus SetActiveCharge(6) on Anamnesis itself; the case requires charge 0 four frames later.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-318]: "dropping and later recovering it can likewise forget the charge it had earned. Its charge must belong to Anamnesis itself across active-item swaps"
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:391-409 sets charge 3, swaps to a fully charged Book of Belial and back (re-added with charge 0) and requires charge 3. Fails in the unchanged starter, so it is target evidence although validation/case-contracts.tsv calls it a guard.

clauses.anchor: Task, sentence 2: "Preserve behaviour outside the reported paths."
clauses.note: 24 preserved cases pass in the unchanged starter. Most observe the composite's other reports, whose repairs the starter already contains, so a fix that breaks them is caught; nothing observes an item, trinket, enemy or character outside the composite's twenty reports.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-217]: "A wounded player with six red-heart containers and two filled hearts is left with one filled heart, while the conversion should empty the red hearts consistently for that capacity."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:994-1002 checks the single reported data point (max=12, red=4 -> red=0, max still 12). It does not probe a second fill level, so capacity-based and empty-everything readings both pass.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-465]: "Birdbath does nothing when used: no bath appears next to Isaac."
Problem, report [#EX-447]: "An enemy standing right next to Isaac when he comes down from the jump takes no damage at all."

clauses.note: Runtime fact added in catalog 5.0.0; no case asserts it on its own.

known_issues: Fixture trap: tragic_mushroom_diminishing (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:343-351) requires the third speed gain to be > 0.05 while the engine clamps MoveSpeed at 2.0. Isaac starts at 1.0 and the first use adds 0.6, so only 0.4 of headroom is left for uses two and three; any valid diminishing series whose second speed gain is >= 0.35 (decay ratio >= ~0.58) reports a third gain <= 0.05 and fails. The reference itself only shows 0.10 instead of its nominal 0.15.

Order dependence: the thirty main-suite cases share one run and one player (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:264-1009). State leaks forward (Forbidden Fruit's +0.99 damage is part of every later damage figure; Mutant Clover is silently replaced by Anamnesis before its reset guard; a pcall failure in any step emits GCB_FATAL and leaves every later case unobserved).

Shared game-log markers (private NOTES.md, Verifier design): results are parsed from unauthenticated `[GCB_CASE]` lines written through Isaac.DebugString into the same log the submission can write to, so outcomes are only meaningful under the honest-code assumption.

Process coupling: the secret-room process runs with continued=true as player_type=18 (James), inheriting the James process's run from Steam's in-memory cache (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/test.sh:85-108). apocryphon_stats and blue_moon are therefore measured on James, who already owns The Apocryphon.

validation/case-contracts.tsv labels eight cases `guard`; two of them (tragic_mushroom_diminishing, anamnesis_charge_persistence) fail in the unchanged starter and are mapped as target here. validation/predicate-matrix.tsv agrees: the EX-303 and EX-318 single-report candidates newly pass them.

Launch harness: this task runs the frozen composite's three suites and test.sh unchanged, but the Hub mounts the task's own tests/run-game.sh over the image's copy. That script queues the launch request as soon as the offline Steam client proper is up, repeats an ignored request once, replaces a client that takes none (up to four starts per game process), and allows longer wall-clock budgets. It decides no case. The image's launch sequence left game processes unstarted on the congested host on 2026-09-23 (UTC); see NOTES.md.
